questions.question: The tiny centre of an atom, where protons and neutrons sit, is called the _____.
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are packed in the nucleus; electrons move around it.

questions.question: Which particle of an atom has a negative charge?
questions.explanation: Electrons carry a −1 charge. Protons are +1, neutrons have no charge, and the nucleus is not a single particle.

questions.question: Is it true that neutrons have a positive charge?
questions.explanation: Neutrons have no charge at all, which is where their name comes from ("neutral"). Protons are the positive ones.

questions.question: The number of protons in an atom is called its _____.
questions.explanation: The atomic number (Z) counts the protons, for example 6 for carbon.

questions.question: Is it true that two atoms with different numbers of protons can be the same element?
questions.explanation: The number of protons defines the element. 6 protons is always carbon; 7 protons is always nitrogen.

questions.question: Why does a neutral atom have the same number of electrons as protons?
questions.answer: Because each proton is +1 and each electron is −1, so equal numbers cancel and the atom has no overall charge.
questions.explanation: Each proton is +1 and each electron is −1. With equal numbers, the charges cancel, so the atom has no overall charge.

questions.question: What does the mass number of an atom count?
questions.explanation: The mass number counts everything in the nucleus. "Only the neutrons" is a common mistake: to get only the neutrons, you must subtract the atomic number.

questions.question: An atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 150" role="img" aria-label="A periodic table tile for Na, with atomic number 11 at the top and mass number 23 at the bottom"><rect x="90" y="10" width="120" height="130" rx="10" fill="#5b7fe0" fill-opacity="0.15" stroke="#5b7fe0" stroke-width="2"/><text x="102" y="36" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor">11</text><text x="150" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="40" font-weight="700" fill="currentColor">Na</text><text x="150" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="currentColor">23</text><text x="84" y="34" text-anchor="end" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#8a94a3">atomic number</text><text x="216" y="126" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#8a94a3">mass number</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12. 23 is tempting, but it counts protons and neutrons together.

questions.question: A neutral atom has 3 protons and 4 neutrons. How many electrons does it have, and why?
questions.figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 120" role="img" aria-label="A nucleus made of 3 orange protons and 4 gray neutrons"><circle cx="90" cy="60" r="44" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/><circle cx="76" cy="48" r="11" fill="#e8792b"/><circle cx="100" cy="46" r="11" fill="#8a94a3"/><circle cx="66" cy="70" r="11" fill="#8a94a3"/><circle cx="90" cy="66" r="11" fill="#e8792b"/><circle cx="114" cy="66" r="11" fill="#8a94a3"/><circle cx="80" cy="86" r="11" fill="#8a94a3"/><circle cx="104" cy="88" r="11" fill="#e8792b"/><circle cx="180" cy="44" r="9" fill="#e8792b"/><text x="196" y="49" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="currentColor">proton</text><circle cx="180" cy="78" r="9" fill="#8a94a3"/><text x="196" y="83" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="currentColor">neutron</text></svg>
questions.answer: 3 electrons, because in a neutral atom the electrons balance the protons; neutrons have no charge and do not change the count.
questions.explanation: In a neutral atom the electrons balance the protons; neutrons have no charge, so they do not change the count. (This atom is lithium.)

questions.question: Is it true that the periodic table orders the elements by increasing atomic number?
questions.explanation: Reading left to right and row by row, each element has one more proton than the one before: H is 1, He is 2, Li is 3…

questions.question: Elements in the same column of the periodic table, called a _____, behave in similar ways.
questions.explanation: A column is a group; a row is a period.

questions.question: Why do elements in the same group react in similar ways?
questions.answer: Because they have the same number of outer electrons, and the outer electrons are what take part in reactions.
questions.explanation: The outer electrons are what take part in reactions. Lithium and sodium both have 1, so both are very reactive.

questions.question: Is it true that almost all of an atom's mass is in its nucleus?
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons are each about 2000 times heavier than an electron, so the electrons add almost nothing to the mass.
